text: Pompey the Great's full Roman name was what?

Why was Pompey's first triumph especially controversial at Rome?
choices: He celebrated it after losing a battle
He was too young and had held no regular magistracy
He was still legally a tribune

text: Pompey and Crassus shared which major office in 70 BCE?

Which slave revolt was brought to its end in the same year Pompey and Crassus became consuls?

Which tribune proposed the law granting Pompey command against the pirates?

After suppressing piracy, Pompey received command in the war against which king?

Which Roman commander had previously fought Mithridates extensively before Pompey replaced him?
Pompey's eastern settlements greatly expanded Roman influence in which broad region?
Which long-standing Hellenistic kingdom did Pompey reduce to a Roman province in 64 BCE?
Pompey intervened in Judaea and entered which city's sanctuary in 63 BCE?
Which Armenian king submitted to Pompey during his eastern campaigns?

When Pompey returned from the East in 62 BCE, what did he do with his army?
Pompey expected the Senate to ratify which of his acts after his eastern victories?
One major domestic goal Pompey pursued after his eastern campaigns was land for whom?
Senatorial resistance to Pompey's settlements helped push him into alliance with Caesar and whom else?
The informal political arrangement of Caesar, Pompey, and Crassus is known as the what?
Pompey's alliance with Caesar was strengthened by Pompey's marriage to which woman?

Caesar's consulship of 59 BCE was important for Pompey chiefly because it secured what for him?
choices: Ratification of settlements and land measures

text: Which stubborn consul tried to obstruct Caesar's measures in 59 BCE and became a foil to the triumvirs?
At the conference of Luca in 56 BCE, Pompey and Crassus agreed to seek which office again?
The meeting at Luca helped renew the political compact among Caesar, Pompey, and Crassus in what year?
After the arrangements following Luca, Pompey received a provincial command in which region?
Pompey governed his Spanish provinces largely through what unusual method?
choices: Through legates while remaining near Rome

text: The death of Julia in 54 BCE weakened Pompey's personal bond with which ally?
Which disaster in 53 BCE removed the third member of the First Triumvirate?
Crassus died fighting which eastern power, leaving Pompey and Caesar increasingly opposed?
Following street violence at Rome, Pompey was appointed sole consul in 52 BCE after the death of whom?

Pompey's appointment as sole consul in 52 BCE was meant chiefly to restore what?

By the late 50s BCE, Pompey increasingly aligned with which broad senatorial tendency?
Which orator often sought Pompey's support while trying to preserve the Republic's senatorial order?
When the crisis with Caesar sharpened, Pompey supported the demand that Caesar do what?
Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon in 49 BCE made Pompey the principal champion of what cause?
choices: The Senate's side in the civil war

text: At the opening of the civil war in 49 BCE, Pompey withdrew from Italy to organize resistance in which region?

Which city in Greece became a major base for Pompey's senatorial coalition before Pharsalus?
Pompey had notable success against Caesar near Dyrrhachium in 48 BCE before the decisive battle at what site?

choices: His signet ring and severed head

text: Pompey's death in Egypt occurred in the same year as which decisive civil-war battle?
Which son of Pompey later became a major naval opponent of Octavian?
Pompey's elder surviving son, who continued resistance in Spain before Munda, was named what?
Which battle in 45 BCE destroyed the last major Pompeian resistance led by Pompey's sons in Spain?
Sextus Pompey's later power base against the triumvirs was centered on which island?

The Curia of Pompey, where Caesar was assassinated, formed part of what larger complex?
Pompey's theater included a temple to which goddess at its summit?
Pompey's career is often cited as evidence that the late Republic increasingly rewarded commanders with what kind of authority?
Which speech by Cicero is especially associated with supporting the grant of Pompey's command against Mithridates?
Pompey's prestige rested heavily on repeated celebration of what quintessential Roman honor?
Which rival reformer of an earlier generation was sometimes compared with Pompey as another dominant man in Republican politics, though from a very different background?
Pompey's relationship with Crassus is best described as what for much of their careers?
choices: Tense rivalry mixed with periodic cooperation

text: When Pompey sought ratification of his eastern settlements, his most principled senatorial opponent was often which stern statesman?
Pompey's dominance in the East involved founding or reorganizing many cities primarily to stabilize what?
Which Roman virtue did Pompey's public image often emphasize through victory, command, and spectacle?
Pompey's special command against piracy is a classic example of Roman fear that ordinary magistracies were too weak to protect what?

Which office did Pompey never permanently transform into a monarchy despite the fears attached to his prominence?

Which Roman region became one of Pompey's earliest proving grounds against Marian forces after Sulla's return?
Pompey's extraordinary rise before holding the full cursus honorum most clearly signaled the weakening of what republican norm?
Which later Roman strongman most directly inherited the political problem of how to combine singular military power with anti-monarchical language after Pompey and Caesar?
Pompey's eastern reorganization helped make Roman relations with client kings a key instrument of rule in which area?
Which enemy of Sulla in Spain was defeated by Pompey only after a long, difficult war in the 70s BCE?
The Sertorian War was fought primarily in which peninsula?
Pompey's mixed performance in Spain against Sertorius showed that his reputation sometimes outpaced his success against what kind of opponent?
Which term best describes the commands Pompey received against pirates and Mithridates when compared with normal yearly magistracies?
Pompey's Senate house within his theater complex later gained grim fame because it was the site of whose assassination?
In late Republican memory, Pompey often appears as Caesar's rival but also as an earlier pioneer of what political pattern?
choices: Rule by extraordinary command backed by personal prestige

text: Which Roman assembly politics helped ambitious leaders like Pompey bypass purely senatorial resistance by courting broader support?
choices: Popular legislation through tribunes and assemblies

text: Pompey's long-term historical significance in the fall of the Republic lies partly in showing that military supremacy no longer fit neatly inside what older framework?
Which label is least accurate for Pompey in the 50s BCE?
Pompey and Caesar moved from alliance to war largely because neither man was willing to accept political vulnerability after giving up what?
The final collapse of Pompey's cause after Pharsalus most immediately benefited which Roman leader?
